not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.

spec:
Publish a long-form, linkable, print-friendly whitepaper on the repository's GitHub-hosted docs path, linked from README, that coins deterministic progressive disclosure: a pure frontier derives each agent's next action and a per-node task card disclosing only that node's prompt, selected policy instructions and inputs from Git state. Explain the mechanism as the reset built it: goal documents on per-goal branches with CAS writes, lease branches, the declarative workflow.json graph with review and human approve nodes, findings and corrections, tree/change identities and fingerprint staleness, stacked PRs with carry-forward, policy branches that pause work, and releases. Include one synthetic end-to-end trace and accessible diagrams, and state limitations candidly (advisory routing, no comprehension proof, what R1-R15 gave up). Claims bind to an explicit engine version and are checked against it. Changed from the old wording: drop heartbeats, receipts, storage locks, linear stacks and model-effort binding, and describe the Release 1 lens-based default graph.

Migrated from GitHub issue #490 after the engine reset (#740).

Write it after G1037, from the engine as released and the private-app dogfood run notes (real goals, a real release, measured costs), and include the git-flow release branching (G1025), capabilities (G1027) and owner-question interviews (G1026).
